subject: Urban Planning
title: Modular Infrastructure: Building Like LEGO
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Modular Infrastructure: Building Like LEGO.

hook.text: China built a 57-story skyscraper in 19 days using prefab modules like building blocks. Infrastructure could work the same way.

buildup.text: Modular infrastructure uses factory-built parts assembled on site. Water plants, power systems, and bridges snap together.

discovery.text: Modular systems cost less, build faster, and can be expanded by adding more modules as demand grows.

twist.text: Traditional infrastructure is designed as a monolith — one massive project. If needs change, the whole thing must be rebuilt.

climax.text: Modular water treatment systems already serve disaster zones and remote communities. The technology is proven at small scale.

punchline.text: Build small. Add more. Scale up as the city grows. Not all at once.

quiz.question: What advantage does modular infrastructure have over traditional monolithic systems?
options: It's stronger because factory conditions produce better quality
It can be expanded incrementally as demand grows, reducing upfront cost
It lasts longer because modules are built with premium materials
